description:
Write, debug and learn Go on iPhone and iPad. GopherForge combines an on-device Go compiler, source editor, tests, an offline React study workflow and a practical learning library. Build, run, test, vet and format with bundled Go 1.27.1, even offline once compatible project sources are present.

CODE AND DEBUG ON DEVICE
• Edit multi-file Go projects, go.mod and web sources with highlighting and keyboard shortcuts.
• Tap a Go line number to set a breakpoint. Run executes normally without breakpoints and automatically starts source debugging when they exist.
• Continue, Step Into, Step Over, Step Out and Stop. Inspect project call stacks, source locations and bounded current-frame local values.
• Breakpoints persist per project. Debug probes stay in a temporary snapshot; saved source is unchanged.
• Follow diagnostics to source and read individual test results, output, Go-generated PNGs and concurrency timelines.
• Create projects, import public GitHub snapshots or Files content, and export your work. Organize projects with favorites, tags, search and a collapsible Files sidebar.

EXPLORE REACT OFFLINE
• Build browser JS, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, CSS and local JSON with bundled esbuild WASI.
• Build from Output with Build & Preview or the documented offline npm commands and fixed React catalog. Open full screen, reload and share the project archive.
• Trace small deterministic in-memory Go APIs through an explicit Gin-compatible adapter and local request replay. No network listener or cloud runtime is used.
• This educational mode has no full Node.js/npm runtime, Bun, arbitrary scripts, Vite plugins or registry downloads. TypeScript is transpiled without type checking. API state is temporary, with up to 64 mutations per session.

LEARN GO AND PREPARE FOR INTERVIEWS
• Follow 186 teaching lessons and 22 prediction challenges across 23 units, including 139 worked readings with code, diagrams, references and understanding checks.
• Study values, collections, interfaces, errors, generics, modules, concurrency, runtime and the standard library.
• Compare Go architectures and clean-code tradeoffs. Explore all 23 classic patterns and six concurrency/resilience patterns.
• Work through JSON v2 contracts, SQL service lifetimes, WaitGroup.Go, synctest and errgroup.
• Learn the environment: Bash, Git, Docker, Kubernetes, MongoDB, Redis and verified workflows with Codex, Claude Code and Cursor in your own native environment.
• Prepare with 92 interview guides, 12 topics, four levels and twelve interactive algorithm labs with 36 scenarios.
• Return with Continue and restored lesson drafts. Course completion, compiler evidence, interview marks, assistance and study places persist locally. Review matches concepts; Fix mistakes explains three-choice answers.

MADE FOR YOUR DEVICE
Native layouts adapt to iPhone, iPad and supported Duo postures. Use touch or external keyboards, theme and text-size settings, extra scroll room, and supported Face ID/passcode locking. One paid download, no subscription, advertising trackers or app account. Projects and progress stay local; a chosen Files/iCloud library follows your provider. App and web progress are separate.

COMPATIBILITY
Go runs in WebAssembly/WASI with bounded memory/output: no guest networking, cgo or general shell. Ordinary Run has no guaranteed CPU Stop. Module ZIP budgets include 4,000 files. Imports and missing Go packages need a connection. Source debugging covers project code, with no watch expressions, conditional breakpoints or vendor/stdlib stepping. Stop needs a project checkpoint. Isolated frontend previews block external requests; legacy local HTML previews may load project-linked resources. Database, deployment and agent lessons teach external native workflows.

Guide: https://gopherforge.app/guide
Support: https://gopherforge.app/support
Privacy: https://gopherforge.app/privacy
promotionalText: Go on your device: automatic breakpoints, offline React builds, tests and Continue. Learn with 186 lessons, 92 interview guides and 12 interactive algorithm labs.

• Added isolated offline React builds with a documented npm command subset, bundled browser packages and full-screen previews.

• Added original React and debugger walkthroughs, updated the app guide and documented supported commands and limits. Existing source, learning progress and Continue remain intact.
• Build & Preview in Output, full-screen and reload controls, local browser/address actions and project archive sharing.

• Safer Files library switching, bookmark restoration, conflict recovery and source-preserving async package operations.
• Exact GitHub commit snapshots, import omission details, strict terminal command validation and expanded lesson explanations.
reviewNotes:
GopherForge 1.3.0 build 48. Educational Go programming environment; no account or demo credentials required. Release automatically after approval.

SOURCE DEBUGGER: Projects > Examples > Source debugger > Source debugger walkthrough > Open. In Build/Code, tap gutter line 12 (result := double(start)), then Run. It pauses before the call with start=3. Step Into enters double at line 6 with n=3. Step Over reaches return with value=6; Step Out returns to line 13 with result=6. Continue finishes with output 6. Stop ends a session at the next own-source checkpoint. Remove breakpoints via the file-header menu to use ordinary Run. Temporary trusted source probes never overwrite saved source. The own-source call stack/current-frame locals are bounded; watches, conditions and stdlib/vendor stepping are not implemented.

OFFLINE REACT: Projects > Examples > Offline frontend > React + Gin study board > Open. Select Terminal, run npm install --offline, then npm run build. Select Output > Open full screen. Add a task, change a filter and inspect/edit the original project sources. Supported npm commands invoke the app's bounded educational builder, not Node/npm or a shell. esbuild WASI and fixed React/React DOM/scheduler sources are bundled in the reviewed binary. No package registry, cloud build, arbitrary scripts, lifecycle hooks, plugins or Bun. TypeScript is transpiled without checking.

ISOLATION: The new frontend uses a nonpersistent WebKit project origin and blocks external HTTP(S), WebSockets, frames, workers and popups. The optional gin-replay recipe allows only explicit local API paths to execute actual Go handlers through httptest inside the existing WASI sandbox. Each request reconstructs deterministic in-memory state using a bounded mutation history; no socket, database or long-running network server is added. The built-in study board uses local JSON fixtures. An external GitHub project was used only in developer interoperability tests and is not bundled in the app.

User Go/React project sources—including imported projects—remain viewable/editable in Files/Code. Imports and missing Go package preparation need a connection; bundled examples/builds do not. The app remains a learning workspace and does not install separate apps or download new compiler/frontend tools at runtime. Projects, breakpoints and progress are local; existing Continue storage is preserved. No subscriptions, IAP, app accounts, ads or analytics SDK added.

Guide with native screenshots and detailed limits: https://gopherforge.app/guide#offline-react
Debugger instructions: https://gopherforge.app/guide#source-debugger
BUILD 48 FOLLOW-UP: React + Gin study board > Open > Run checks Go routes. Output then offers Build & Preview, which installs from the bundled catalog and builds locally. Full-screen and Reload stay inside the isolated viewer. Share project exports a snapshot; it does not publish code. Legacy static sites additionally offer the actual loopback browser address; the UI states its device-only lifetime.

Lessons restore editable drafts and pre-solution source; Practice is directly accessible. Files libraries preserve separate source across switches and relaunches. A physical iPhone local Files-provider A/B edit/relaunch test passed in an isolated QA bundle; remote iCloud sync is not claimed. Ordinary Run does not guarantee a CPU deadline or tight-loop Stop. The app makes no new account, server or network-runtime requirement.
